correctness.rationale: Uniform-prefix / sorted-suffix conditional coupling yields exact descent/inversion means and an exact covariance one half of the conditional expected descents. The covariance proof resolves both internal adjacent comparisons and the boundary minimum event. The law of total covariance plus monotone conditional means proves the strict finite sign. On fixed k/n->a, a bounded one-dependent triangular array and a first-order degenerate-kernel decomposition give asymptotically independent internal Gaussian fluctuations; occupancy count CLT supplies the common normal factor. The resulting explicit covariance matrix is derived from exact derivatives of conditional means. Exact rational program check.py passed 75033 assertions and an independently simulated finite diagnostic agrees; finite evidence is supporting only. The restrictions deck sizes at least two and positive shuffle counts and fixed positive critical parameter are explicit.

originality.rationale: The main 2026 random-to-top paper gives conditional decomposition and separate marginal CLTs, but no finite joint covariance or bivariate critical covariance. The 2025 joint inversion/descent paper concerns uniform permutations, which have vanishing limiting correlation, and supplies no shuffle occupancy mixture. A positive common-occupancy limit does not follow from separate normal limits or uniform permutation covariance alone. Record and literature searches found no covering claim, subject to ordinary historical-priority limits.

value.rationale: Marginal shuffle statistics are inadequate to quantify their joint discriminatory power. The exact positive finite-time dependence identity supplies a nontrivial universal sign, and the explicit Gaussian cross-covariance isolates a shared occupancy source of dependence that is absent in uniform permutations. The result is motivated by the parent paper’s two separate asymptotic tests, not by an arbitrary invariant or parameter slice. It does not assert mixing-time improvements or general joint tail behavior.
